walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Landscapes in the UK — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Landscapes in the UK brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Landscapes in the UK.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which line divides upland and lowland Britain?
options: Watford Line
Tees-Exe Line
Hadrian's Wall
Severn-Trent Line

mcqs.q: Where are softer sedimentary rocks found in UK?
options: Scottish Highlands
Southeast England
Snowdonia
Lake District

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.
Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mitigation and adaptation to climate change?
options: Mitigation reduces the causes (cutting greenhouse gas emissions); adaptation reduces the impacts (e.g. building sea walls, drought-resistant crops, early warning systems).
Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Mitigation and adaptation mean the same thing — both are about stopping climate change.

mcqs.q: Why does longshore drift move sediment in only one direction along a coast?
options: Longshore drift only happens during storms.
The prevailing wind drives swash diagonally up the beach at an angle, but gravity-driven backwash returns sediment straight downhill — creating net movement in the swash direction.
Longshore drift moves sediment back and forth with the tide.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
